body.statement: The tuple \(\theta^{\pm}\) is generated by an acyclic positive-structural-noise, positive-measurement-noise Gaussian SCM satisfying every member condition of \(\mathcal M_{3,2,2}\) except nonnegative variance shifts, with true target set \(\{1,2\}\); its transformed second target block is \(\operatorname{diag}(-1/2,0)\), so the entrywise-nonnegative ordered certificate rejects that true target.  The tuple \(\theta^{\mathrm{split}}\) satisfies every member condition except the common-reference restriction, with true target set \(\{1,2\}\), but its reference shift has rank one and no size-two reference principal block is positive definite.  Thus signed shifts destroy the nonnegative-diagonal necessity, while absence of a common reference destroys the rank-\(r\) carrier and the range-reconstruction step; an extension would require, respectively, baseline-variance feasibility inequalities or an aggregate carrier built from several environments.
body.justification: The result identifies exactly which parts of the certificate fail when either design restriction is removed.
body.gap: BACKSHIFT permits signed covariance changes and does not require a designated common reference, whereas the labeled principal-block fiber uses both restrictions; the explicit witnesses prevent that narrower result from being advertised as a general covariance-shift characterization.
body.consumer: Panel designers learn whether to add a lowest-variance baseline and a broad calibration environment, and analysts without them know which certificate component must be replaced rather than trusted.
